jobs.description: Do you enjoy working with technology and building complex products? As an Assembly Technician, you will work on advanced electromechanical systems within an innovative high-tech production environment. You will join an international organization where technology, quality, and collaboration are at the heart of everything. Together with your colleagues, you will assemble modules and systems that are used worldwide in advanced technological applications. What’s your job about? As an Assembly Technician, you will be responsible for assembling complex technical systems and modules. You ensure that products are built accurately according to technical drawings, specifications, and work instructions. Your responsibilities include: Assembling mechanical and electromechanical modules and systems. Working according to technical drawings, schematics, and assembly instructions. Building cabinets, subassemblies, and technical components. Performing measurements and quality inspections. Identifying deviations and contributing to process improvements. Collaborating with colleagues from production, engineering, and quality departments. Ensuring products meet the highest quality standards. You will work in a two-shift schedule: Morning shift: 06:00 – 14:15 Afternoon shift: 14:15 – 23:00 (Friday: until 20:30) What skills do you have? We are looking for a motivated technician with an eye for detail and an interest in high-tech manufacturing. Affinity with technology, assembly, or production. Experience assembling machines, modules, or technical products is a plus. Ability to read technical drawings or willingness to learn. Strong attention to detail and quality. A proactive and hands-on attitude. Sense of responsibility and ownership. Good communication skills in English. What do you get in return? A position within an innovative high-tech organization. A gross monthly salary between €3.300 and €3.600, including shift allowance. Extensive training and development opportunities. Careegrowth possibilities within production, technology, or engineering. A modern and professional working environment. An international and collaborative team culture. Competitive employment conditions. You will join a leading high-tech manufacturing organization in the Eindhoven region. The company develops and produces advanced technological systems and modules that are used worldwide in industries such as semiconductors, healthcare, industrial automation, and mobility. Innovation, quality, and continuous improvement are central to the organization. Employees are encouraged to take initiative, develop their technical skills, and build a long-term career within a dynamic international environment.

Tasks, salary, and working through Charlie works  30 September 2026 4 min read What exactly does a logistics worker do? Do you want to know what a logistics worker does before you start working in the Netherlands? In short, a logistics worker ensures that products end up in the right place. This starts with unloading trucks and ends with preparing orders for shipment. A lot happens in between: scanning, sorting, packing, and sometimes driving a pallet truck or forklift. The job is physical, varied, and very suitable if you enjoy working with your hands. You do not need a diploma, and basic English or Polish is often sufficient on the work floor. That is why this is a popular first job for migrant workers from Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, and Romania. What is a logistics worker? A logistics worker usually works in a warehouse or distribution center. You are part of a team that manages the flow of goods. Think of large centers for webshops, supermarkets, or transport companies. There are thousands of these types of locations in the Netherlands, especially around Venlo, Tilburg, Rotterdam, and Utrecht. The role is broad. One day you pick orders, the next you help in the packing department or check the stock. Do you want to know more about what such a location looks like from the inside? Then read our article about working in a distribution center in the Netherlands . The main tasks at a glance Tasks vary by company, but these are the most common activities: - Order picking : removing products from the shelves using a handheld scanner or voice-picking system. - Packing : preparing orders for shipment, including labels and shipping documents. - Loading and unloading : filling or emptying trucks, often with a pallet truck. - Checking stock : counting and registering whether everything in the system is correct. - Forklift driving : moving pallets (you need a certificate for this). - Sorting : distributing packages by destination or rout...
